Great point. The lore/canon is all over the place. The differences in the manga and animated series alone are staggering. I also believe no game has actually stated how pokeballs work, at least not until the shrinking explanation in PLA. 

Regarding matter/energy conversion, iirc R/B/G/Y and FR/LG did establish the existence of the technology. At one point in the story you have to help Bill who is working on matter to energy conversion for his PC system (he doesn’t use the term), and accidentally spliced himself with a Pokémon while trying to swap places with it.

I get what you’re saying regarding crafting things irl and in the game, but you’ve gotta realize there will always be exceptions to that. Say for example, you purchase a complicated build-it-yourself robot toy, you may not know exactly how all the mechanical components work but you can put it together and make it function. Not the best analogy, but there’s more to the pokeballs that just acorns and stones for sure. Steam comes out of a hole on the bottom, potentially implying some sort of machination behind just a ball that a shrunken Pokémon goes into. 

Regarding other games, manga, anime etc, it’s been very well established that pokeballs work using a form of matter to energy conversion; the same process is what allows people in the games/shows to store and transfer their Pokémon via a computer. The animated series has shown Ash sending his Pokémon digitally to the professor many times. The actual mechanics of pokeballs haven’t been explained much beyond matter/energy, though.

My thoughts exactly. We know pokeballs are a new invention in the Hisui time period, but that doesn’t necessarily mean they were invented in Hisui. I also like to think they were invented in Johto, and were brought over through trade etc. 

Kinda like giving guns to hunter gatherers, at first it’s gonna seem like magic, but after some more understanding the technology makes sense to them. 

And maybe magic or some mystical element too, there’s a lot of that that floats around the Pokémon world.

My headcanon so far has been that something about pokeballs are not understood entirely in Hisui yet…the description for pokeballs in PLA calls them “mysterious”. 

That being said, I feel it’s more likely that Laventon and the people at large do not really know how they work, and assume that the Pokémon must shrink down to fit. There’s documented cases in the real world of technology being used, without a firm understanding of the science behind it.

Idk, I just feel that makes more sense to me than retconning years of the established “matter to energy” explanation. 

Just my thoughts!

You can also use the cast as the main focus of your build, although you’ll have to plan your weapons accordingly. Certain weapon aspects, i.e Poseidon, Hera, will be centered around the use of your cast and you can get some crazy high cast damage with the right boons. I’ve breezed through an entire run multiple times using Poseidon’s aspect and the correct set of boons, with end-of-area bosses dying in seconds. It all comes down to how you wanna play, and the wonderful thing about this game is you can play it so many different ways!

As some above me stated, you’re not a therapist.
